records.description: No. First of all. The Padawan is not named after Star Wars. The similarity of names is pure, though by no means undesirable, coincidence. Padawan means "Pale Ale doing alright without a name" and was chosen as the beer name for an unnamed Bierol Pale Ale in an online vote in 2014. Today, The Padawan is not only already a classic but also the No. 1 in the core range. And there is a reason for this: The Padawan is incredibly fruity, incredibly velvety and has everything a Pale Ale needs: The right dose (which is of course not exactly small) of high-quality hops, a fine, almost creamy mouthfeel, a slender amber-colored body and a bit dry in the finish. But above all: mango. In the nose, on the palate, and it lingers. For a long time. Really long. Sparkling, fresh, lean and with a distinct bitterness. By no means just a summer beer. Our favorite beer of all!

records.description:
Use of Pale Ale malt and three hop varieties (Cascade, Hallertau Tradition, Callista), as well as Nottingham Ale yeast.
Pale ale is one of the oldest light beer styles in the world - originally brewed in England at the beginning of the 18th century, this top-fermented specialty has continued to evolve. The variety is characterized by a balanced hop bitterness/aroma mixture.
For this year's Saxon interpretation, we use the hop varieties Mosaic and Smaragd
- a refreshing beer suitable for summer! Original wort: 11.7°

records.description: In the beer world, the "ale" is the younger cousin of the older, more grown-up "lager". When conceptualizing this particular beer, the goal was to create a similar drinking experience to that of their flagship lager. While it looks and feels like the lager, the flavor is as unique as possible. Their spin on a traditional golden ale, the blonde ale is a very light, refreshingly crisp beer. Made with a very simple malt bill to accentuate a much more complex flavor profile. Their blonde ale is bursting with citrus notes, from the generous amounts of Cascade, Amarillo, and Citra hops used throughout the process.

records.description:
A compound and fused culture saison brewed in collaboration with the elegant and dandy men of FOREST & MAIN.

Starting with an undecorated grist of extra pale base malt, oats and wheat flakes producing an uncomplicated structure for a complex build.
A free rise fermentation using a classic farmhouse saison strain is then blended with 3 separate wild barrel fruit cultures.

A 5 month fermentation / maturation period leaves us with a spritzed up funky midsummer smasher.
Blooming with crisp, clean cider barrel esters followed by a compounded admixture of acidic fresh orchard fruits.

Crab apple, white grape, peach flesh and tart lime zest intermingle with aseptic farmyard tannins resulting in a crisp and bracing sunshine quencher.

The Almighty is crafted with paramount attention to detail and admiration for what came before it. It builds upon our past by encompassing years of toil, representing the legacy we wish to leave behind and the magic we aspire to continue as long as we are able. Most importantly, we craft it to live up to the goodwill you have granted us since our earliest days. The Julius family is a cornerstone to our endeavors at Tree House, endeavors that have seen us through hardship, friendship, life, and business in ways we could not have imagined starting out. We can't fathom a better way to celebrate eleven fortunate years than with this progressive beer representing the Tree House spirit at its core. We hope you enjoy it in good health and good spirits, and we thank you for your fervent support of our brewery.

records.description: I brewed an American Pale Ale - Beneficiaries of Chance - in celebration of marrying the love of my life, Lauren (aka Tree House L-Dog). On the eve of our first anniversary, I brewed another beer for Lauren, In Perpetuity. It hopes to celebrate foreverness - in love, passion, and regardless of circumstance - the notion that what is good and beloved will last forever. In Perpetuity is brewed with a simple malt bill and two of my favorite hops - Citra, and Nelson. It pours a hazy bright orange in the glass and mixes notes of tropical fruit with a strong citrus backbone. Soft, and eminently drinkable. I hope you enjoy it.

records.description: The India Pale Ale gets its name from the beer that the English shipped to India in the 17th century when drinking water was risky at best. For the long journey across multiple oceans, the English would throw large amounts of hops into the barrels of beer to prevent spoilage, because hops are a natural anti-septic. Flash forward 400 years and that necessary process is now one of the most popular beer "styles" in the world. As a tribute to the original English and modern American IPA styles, their IPA is a combination of smooth body and robust flavor profile. Darker in color, this India Pale Ale malt bill offers a very interesting mouthfeel balance. A specific blend of Centennial, Cascade, Columbus, Simcoe, and Amarillo hops present an incredible aroma followed by intense piney and citrus flavor.

records.description: Wanderer is our unfiltered German-style Helles Lager. A meticulous, highly technical beer brewed utilizing traditional techniques and ingredients, Wanderer is crisp, bright, and immensely enjoyable. Wanderer pours a brilliant straw gold color in the glass with a puffy, bright white foam. It carries a flavor profile of doughy malts, light straw, clean lager yeast, and just the right dash of zippy noble hops. Beers that command your attention are a wonderful thing. Beers that can fade into the background and sort of be an unspoken companion to celebratory moments in life are also a wonderful thing and deserve to be held in equally high esteem. As a crisp, highly drinkable, and beautifully executed beer, Wanderer fits this profile beautifully.

Enjoy this mellow and deep beer that time has woven together.

It's the summation of almost 15 years of refinement of our unique style of hoppy beer!

records.description: Kölsch is a traditional German style of beer that originated in the Cologne area. However, being a product with a protected geographical indication, in order to be able to bear the name Kölsch, the beer must be produced within a radius of 50 KM around Cologne. That's why we simply call her "Blonde." For this beer we use malt brought from N-V Germany and yeast right from a small factory in Cologne. The beer you hold in your hand is fermented and matured naturally until it reaches the specific, light and refreshing taste.

Saison was originally brewed during the off-season from winter to spring for summer farming. The hops were used to improve preservation, making this style of beer stand out among Belgian beers.

The IBU is a little lower than a regular IPA, around 50, but the dry body and balance make it moderately (!?) bitter. It is bitter.

The Saison yeast gives it a dryness that makes you not feel the alcohol content, and a fruity character that is not unpleasant.

The hops are mainly new varieties from New Zealand and the US. It has a refreshing aroma reminiscent of blue citrus fruits.

Alcohol percentage : 7.0%.

Beer Style : Belgian IPA

records.description: Collaboration with Hoppebräu friendship. For us that means: spending a great time together. Or translated into the best English, a hammer time. Or to quote from MC Hammer's catchy tune while dancing, U can't touch this. We have such a friendship with Hoppebräu from the tranquil Waakirchen in Bavaria. Markus brewed his first brew in Schwoich. The taste is then further fruity, complemented by herbal notes, straight, rather dry and with a pleasant but present bitterness.

records.description: The Double India Pale Ale or DIPA was born out of the modern American concept that "bigger is better". While sometimes true, the most important tenant when it comes to beer is always balance. It is paramount to remember all ingredients are never equal and going big on hops is not the same as going big on grain. Therefore, the intent of this incredible beer was to create a beer that was big in alcohol and flavor but still remarkably drinkable in a tropical climate. Everything about this beer is BIG! From its soft mouthfeel to its exploding hop flavor, this beer excites the senses. Although this beer is over 8% ABV, the intense blend of citrus and passionfruit flavor profiles makes this beer dangerously drinkable.

"Baby Sour" A traditional berliner weisse. A low calorie beer, sour and refreshing, with a hit of roasted coffee. Werk Coffee Roaster's signature blend "Baby" was used to maximise the coffee character with the sourness.
The brewing process of kettle souring added its individuality to the acidity and the deep sweetness of Werk's signature coffee blend, "Baby", and the single origin beans (Colombia El Paraiso Lychee, India Attikan Kent Natural, Costa Rica Santa Teresa).
Enjoy the subtle aroma of freshly roasted coffee, followed by a sourness that hightens your taste buds, and finishing with a smooth coffee mouthfeel.

Lager is the most popular and consumed style of beer in the world. Their flagship lager offers a crisp, clean drinking experience. With the freshest Amarillo and El Dorado hops on to balance out the refreshing all-grain malt bill, this combination is truly a craft.

Designed to remind the Filipino drinker of the beer they grew up drinking, the Engkanto lager is as refreshing as it is flavorful, making it appropriate for any type of occasion in any climate. What makes this beer exciting is that it blends a traditional style with new world hops to blast the palate with citrus aroma and flavor, reminiscent of tropical fruit and lime zest.

records.description:
Can there ever be enough permutations of the great India Pale Ale style? Of course not. In this beautifully nuanced, Japanese esthetic-influenced ale, we marry in the conditioning tank ample dosages of earthy-herbal dry hops (Hersbrucker, Styrian Golding, Santiam) with deft additions of whole leaf Shizuoka green tea. The result of this international botanical marriage is, in a word, sublime.
Baird Beer, as you know, is unfiltered and the addition of whole leaf green tea to Wabi-Sabi IPA has contributed a very strong particle sediment. Do not fear or fret, this is all-natural good stuff and it tastes great! You will not find this in a can or mug of your favorite industrial brew.

records.description: The stylistic origins of the Pale Ale can be found in 18th century Europe, with what is now more commonly referred to as a "bitter". Engkanto decided that it was time to flip that expected traditional style, and their efforts gave birth to the Engkanto Pale Ale. The only way to articulate this drinking experience is flavor. Their Pale Ale presents a very "sessionable" drinking experience, beginning with a strong citrus aroma, followed by a soft, yet complex malt bill, and ending with an exceptionally balanced hop flavor. The overall character of the beer is highlighted by candy-like citrus and passionfruit flavor that is remarkably refreshing.

records.description: Cantillon Gueuze is the Belgian beer par excellence - a perfect blend of one, two and three year old lamb. Tart and slightly sour, Cantillon Gueuze is the real champagne among beers. It is fermented only with wild air yeast from the Brussels Senne valley and matured in centuries-old oak barrels. It is also certified organic in Belgium. A true world classic that will inspire true beer connoisseurs. During late winter and early spring, the Cantillon family brewers will match and blend one, two and three year old lambic for a balanced texture and flavor. In general, the younger lambic is thinner, livelier, and milder on the palate; the older lambic is harder, more complex and penetratingly sour. However, the beer in each barrel is unique, and one three year old lambic can be radically different in taste from another. There is no formula for mixing and no expectation of year-to-year consistency. Brewmaster Jean-Pierre Van Roy simply says that he hopes for the same "harmony" every time. The artfully blended lambic is immediately bottled, and another miraculous event occurs: the mixture of lambic from several different barrels triggers a second fermentation in the bottle. This is the essence of the méthode champenoise from which champagne is made. The end product is called "Gueuze". A few months in the bottle "condition" the beer - it forms carbonic acid, concentrates and organizes the aromas. Under the right storage conditions, fermentation in the bottle will last for years. records.description:
Maris Otter, rolled wheat and a well-measured dose of Munich and Carared malts lay down a runway of warm, rounded toasty notes and give ample support to let the new seasons hop characters take flight.
Loral, Cryo Mosaic, and Citra sourced from our great friends at the legendary Loftus Farms in Moxee, Washington sends aloft notes of light passionfruit, mango, rockmelon, and blueberries. Hints of sweet jasmine and potpourri swoop and swirl in and around candy notes that compliment the rich warm malt tones and touch down for a perfect landing with a satisfyingly balanced finish.

records.description: We always search for exceptional pairings with each of our beers. The Orange Blossom Belgian Blonde is a light-to-medium bodied Belgian-Style Blonde Ale which showcases notes of apricot, orange rock candy and honeysuckle. We love seafood, and our team has found that this beer pairs perfectly with a number of preparations of fish dishes. You'll find this Blonde Ale paired in The Dining Room with our seared black cod, in The Bar with our fried whole black bass, and at Moody Tongue Sushi with our madai nigiri with orange zest and sea salt.

records.description:
Our newest core range IPA is here!

We’ve had some amazing feedback to our last few hazy IPA’s and we realised it’s long overdue that we add one to our permanent range of beers. Utilising what we learned over the past few years we’ve brewed what we feel is the ideal fridge filling hazy IPA. Packed full of some of our favourite new wave hops and fermented with a fruity aroma packed yeast strain. Idaho 7 and Nelson sauvin from New Zealand deliver big tropical, grapefruit flavours while an addition of strata hops finishes off the flavour profile with a little hop dankness. Built on a base of oats and pale malts for a fluffy fruity finish. Grab one, watch the sunset and enjoy a modern full flavoured IPA

records.description: Who is this El Patrón actually? Not the evil drug lord from Colombia, but the one who is the inspiration for this beer. That will remain a secret forever! But what remains a mystery is the similarity to the character of this Double India Pale Ale. Because what comes through on the nose, tongue and palate is powerful. A strong, full-bodied representative of the style. Incredibly creamy and velvety, actually even somehow gentle. And yet El Patrón quickly shows what it can do. On the nose, it has captivating tropical passion fruit notes, a little honey and vanilla, which soon give way to grassy-green hop aromas in the first sip. A full body that is paired with a strong bitterness at the end. And then there's the alcohol. Yes, you can feel it too. This beer moves through the impressions like a wave. Sometimes quiet, sometimes loud, sometimes soft, sometimes hard. But always powerful. Just like El Patrón.

records.description: The Hitachino Nest Espresso Stout is deep black and has a slightly oily consistency. The foam of this Japanese stout is a hit and a dream for any stout lover. With large volume, a fine-pored consistency and a dreamlike brownish color he beautifies the sight of the beer. A scent as you would expect, intense coffee, espresso, mocha and cocoa flavors enchant the nose. In the background subtle smoke nuances come into play. In the Antrunk spreads a fine bitterness of roasted aromas and reminiscent of dark chocolate. A strong flavor of cocoa enchants from the middle and lets the intense flavor of espresso, coffee and mocha go first. At the finish, the espresso notes increase even more and the bitterness becomes a bit more succinct. A taste that has something of a cold espresso. The intense aromas are literally sticking to your tongue and letting this wonderful stout linger in your mouth for a long time. The Hitachino Nest Espresso Stout is a must-have for any Stout lover.

records.description: Tribute is a new beer made in an old style. The Barley Wines of the old days back to the days of yore when a special 'heavy' ale was needed. Tribute is brewed by hand using Elizabethan 'Doubleword Mashing' process that yields very high gravity word. In this process the mashing and sparging process yields a normal beer is repeated a second time. The second mash and sparge is done using the word collected from the first mash instead of water. This concentrated word is said to have a long time to come. The result is a mellow, warming ale with layers of biscuit, roasted hazelnut and maple syrup, with hints of black current and toast.

records.description:
Stout beers are a variety of Porter, which were first brewed in London around 1730. Porter beers were always dark and the name refers to its popularity with street and river porters. It quickly became popular with the working classes. Porter was the first beer style that conquered the world by the end of the 18th century. Somewhere along the line, porter drinkers added the adjective ‘stout’ to Porter when ordering, referring to the strong Porter beer. Eventually, the name Stout became slang for strong dark beer.

The Tale version of this historical beer is extraordinary, as it is the strongest found in the region and the only one in Africa using Ghana cocoa in the brewing process. Adding in rice alongside with roasted barley and malt, this top fermented Cocoa Stout is much more drinkable than typical bitter stouts.

Tale 8 or Black Tale has a surprising aroma and invites you to discover its delicate chocolate and coffee notes followed by a touch of sweet bitterness.
